Subject: Private VPC reference diagrams & deployment cadence (control-plane / data-plane)

Paul — attaching a first-cut of our reference diagrams and a proposed deployment cadence for the on-prem private VPC. The main things we want feedback on from EdgeCloud:

- Control plane placement and reachability (management plane vs. tenant-facing data path).
- Telemetry & observability egress (where should Prom/OTLP/STATSD exit to your SRE fabric).
- KV cache locality for low tail-latency vs. multi-rack redundancy.
- Cutover cadence (canary groups, stagger windows, rollback triggers).

Attachments: vpc_reference_v1.pdf (diagrams), deploy_cadence_v1.xlsx (staging -> canary -> prod timeline).

Specific asks: could you confirm whether your colo has an allowed egress path for 443/4318 to our telemetry collectors, and whether you can accept an inbound control-plane mTLS endpoint on a /26 from our side?

If it's easier, happy to set a 30m sync — suggested times below in calendar invite link.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private VPC reference diagrams & deployment cadence (control-plane / data-plane)

Mateo — thanks for the diagrams, useful level of detail. A few quick notes from SRE before we dig in:

1) Egress: We can allow 443 and OTLP (4318) outbound from the tenant VLANs to your collectors, but it needs to be pinned to the expected FQDNs and our ACLs need the list of IPs for collectors. We cannot open wide CIDR egress.
2) Inbound control-plane: our edge fabric accepts mutually authenticated TLS; allocating a /26 for you is possible but we prefer a /28 for admin endpoints and NAT for ephemeral control-plane clients. We need to coordinate with networking to confirm the reachability window.
3) KV cache locality: recommend keeping a local L1 cache colocated with inference nodes, and a cross-rack replication group for failover. That minimizes cross-rack tail latency but requires periodic warm-up during canaries.

I attached our ops doc that explains accepted egress patterns and the change window requirements.

We can meet tomorrow morning 10:30-11:00 PT if that works — will bring the network engineer.

-Paul
Paul Liu
EdgeCloud Systems — Solutions Engineering

Subject: Re: Private VPC reference diagrams & deployment cadence (control-plane / data-plane)

Following up with some internal clarifications to make the diagram actionable for the network team:

- Control plane endpoints: we'll expose a small set (3) of HA mTLS endpoints in the control cluster. These will be reachable over the admin lane. The control-plane API is management-only; no consumer inference traffic goes there.
- Data plane: inference nodes will issue outbound connections to model-serving backends and the L1 KV cache is in-process or sidecar depending on host type. Cross-rack replication will use an ephemeral overlay VLAN and keep-alive pings to avoid cold starts.
- Observability: prefer having a dedicated telemetry egress IP set (static) that EdgeCloud can ACL — reduce blast radius and make packet flows auditable.

Action items I can take before the sync:
- Add explicit list of collector FQDNs + IPs to the deploy_cadence spreadsheet.
- Annotate the reference diagram with the NAT/masquerade points for tenant-initiated telemetry egress.
- Draft a canary rollback playbook (3-step) to attach to the cadence.

Kim — can you confirm KMS/HSM key hosting constraints for the on-prem package and whether we need to add an HSM rotation window to the cadence?

Jonas Weber
